name: Sign on to the servicing console
description: Sign on to the MERIDIAN CORE servicing console as operator teller1 at branch WEST-014. Set the operator ID, the password and the branch dropdown explicitly -- the branch must be selected even though the form opens on a different default. Submit the sign-on form and land on the main menu. Then read back the branch code the console shows in the status line at the foot of the screen, which confirms which branch the session is bound to.

target.described_as: Read branch code from status line, anchored on fixed label 'BR'
target.rationale: Anchored on the row containing 'BR' rather than an absolute row index, so inserting or reordering rows does not read the wrong value.

steps.intent: Go to the MERIDIAN CORE servicing console sign-on page

target.rationale: The control has no accessible name, so role+name cannot address it at all. It is identified the way an operator does: by the visible label 'Operator ID:' in the same table row. A following-cell variant covers layouts where the label and control are siblings rather than row-mates. A structural selector on name='operator' is appended last: brittle by nature, but on surfaces this hostile it is sometimes the only thing left, and replay records when it is the strategy that had to be used.

checkpoint.description: 'OPERATOR SIGN ON' is present after enter_operator_id.

Control exposes role 'button' with accessible name 'Sign On'; that pair tracks what the control means rather than how it is built, so it leads. Visible text is kept as a fallback in case the role changes but the wording does not.

signals.description: The host returned its Record Not Found screen. This is the injected fault (?inject=notfound) and the wording used when a record is missing at the point of retrieval rather than at search time.
signals.message: No member record matches the supplied identifier.

signals.description: A member search completed and matched no records.

detect.text: No member records matched your search

signals.message: No member record matches the supplied identifier.

signals.description: The host returned its Transaction Rejected screen. This is the injected validation fault (?inject=validation).
signals.message: The host rejected the transaction as entered.

signals.description: The host refused the transfer as entered -- most often insufficient available balance in the source share.

detect.text: The transaction could not be validated

signals.message: The host refused the transfer as entered and no funds moved. This is an answer to the request, not a breakdown of the automation.

signals.description: The host refused one or more submitted field values as malformed.
signals.message: The host rejected the values submitted. Nothing was changed; the individual reasons are listed on the screen.

signals.description: The operator profile is not entitled to this function.

detect.text: is not authorized to perform this

signals.message: This function needs a supervisor profile. Classified as an outcome rather than a failure because the caller can act on it -- re-invoke with supervisor credentials -- whereas escalating to a human would not help unless that human is themselves a supervisor.

signals.description: Unscheduled maintenance notice blocking the flow.

dismiss.described_as: the Continue link on the maintenance interstitial
dismiss.rationale: Dismissal control for the maintenance notice. Identified by role and name because the same word labels a submit button elsewhere in this application.

signals.message: Dismissed the maintenance notice and retried the step.

The servicing session ended mid-flow. Re-authenticating unattended is deliberately not automated: it would mean holding and replaying operator credentials outside the invocation that supplied them, and a blind retry against an unknown rejection risks locking the profile. A human re-establishes the session and hands control back.

signals.description: The host returned an unhandled fault page.
signals.message: The application returned an unexpected fault. The page carries a reference code for the help desk; nothing about the flow can be assumed from here, so the run stops.

signals.description: The supplied operator credentials were refused.
signals.message: Sign-on was refused. Treated as a hard failure rather than a business outcome: the caller supplied credentials that do not work, which is a fault in the invocation rather than an answer about a member. Not escalated, because a human operator cannot fix credentials the caller passed in.

success.description: Goal reached: 'MAIN MENU' is on screen.
